# Motion

> Generates a set of motion tokens for a design system: named easings — cubic-bezier
> or spring — each with its own duration, a derived and deliberately faster exit, a
> per-motion stagger, and purpose aliases that map components onto them. Exports to
> CSS, Tailwind v4, Framer Motion and DTCG, with the cost of each conversion measured
> rather than hidden.

Free, no account, no API key, no rate limit. Every set is a pure function of the URL,
so the same link always returns the same tokens.

Site: https://www.springs.studio

## Using this as a tool

Fetch the page. The motion set is in the HTML — no JavaScript required.

  https://www.springs.studio/

Two readable blocks sit at the end of the document:

  <script type="application/json" id="motion-studio-tokens">  structured data
  <pre>                                                       the same set as text

For JSON alone, swap the path:

  https://www.springs.studio/api/tokens

Both accept the same query string, so a share link works on either.

## Query contract

Every parameter is optional. With none, you get the shipped default set.

  e    Repeated once per motion. Six fields, separated by "*":
         id*name*easing*durationMs*exit*staggerMs
       easing is either
         b.<x1>.<y1>.<x2>.<y2>   cubic-bezier, values x100
         s.<stiffness>.<damping>.<mass>.<velocity>
       exit is either
         r<percent>   a share of the entrance, e.g. r70
         a<ms>        an absolute duration, e.g. a140
  pu   Repeated. Which motion a purpose points at: <purpose>.<entryId>
  xt   Tokens held out of the export: <entryId>*<enter|exit>, "." between entries
  tol  Spring sampling tolerance for the CSS linear() approximation, 1–2000
       (thousandths). Default 10, i.e. 1%.

Purposes: state, dropdown, tooltip, list, drawer, modal, toast

## What comes back

Each motion publishes two tokens:

  motion.<slug>.enter
  motion.<slug>.exit

and each purpose aliases one of them:

  motion.<purpose>-enter -> var(--motion-<slug>-enter)

## Rules that matter when applying these

- Prefer the purpose aliases or the named motions over raw durations.
- Exits stay faster and flatter than entrances. That asymmetry is deliberate;
  symmetric motion reads as sluggish on the way out.
- Ship the prefers-reduced-motion block. It is already in the CSS export.
- A spring has no duration. The `durationMs` on a spring token is a settling
  estimate, not a fact — copying it onto a CSS transition will not reproduce the
  motion. Use the sampled `linear()` in the token's `css` field, or the spring
  parameters with a runtime that does real physics.
- CSS cannot run spring physics, so springs are sampled into a `linear()`
  polyline. `conversionCost.css` in the JSON reports the worst-case error across
  the set, measured against the exact closed-form curve.
- DTCG has no spring type. `$value` carries a linear fallback and the real
  parameters travel in `$extensions["studio.motion.spring"]`.
